Bernie Sanders:
Trump took over the Republican Party and turned it into a right-wing extremist party, to some degree a white nationalist party, whose goal was more and more power for the leader, a cult of the individual toward the leader. Trump says jump, they say how high.
The politics are often racist, divisive. We're supposed to hate that person. We hate that person. We hate Canada. We hate undocumented people. We hate trans people. That is kind of that ideology.
That's not the old Republican Party.

Bernie Sanders on Europe:
The Labour Party is in terrible shape. The French Socialist Party, I don't know what's left of them. The German Social Democratic Party is in bad shape.
If government does not respond to the concerns and needs of people, people lose faith in democracy.

Bernie Sanders:
Right now, to get Medicare, you've got to be 65. We lower it to 55. We include all of the children. We expand Medicare to cover dental, hearing and vision.
Then we go down the next year to 45, then to 35, then everybody is in.

Bernie Sanders:
At a time when the billionaire class is doing phenomenally well, it is appropriate that we impose upon them a wealth tax.
The bill that I've introduced is a 5% annual tax just on billionaires, about 2,000 individuals, not a whole lot of people.
That would raise approximately $400 billion a year, $4 trillion for 10 years.
With that $400 billion, this is what we could do: wipe out childhood poverty. We could have universal and free childcare.
We could provide a $3,000 stipend in the first year to every working-class individual in the country under $150,000.
We can make public colleges and universities tuition-free. We could build 7 million units of low-income and affordable housing.

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey:
The invention of precision-guided bombs has made a lot of old-school bombing campaign techniques completely irrelevant and seemingly barbaric.
The things that the United States and our allies did during World War II today would be considered war crimes because we've become so good at precision-targeted warfare.

Bernie Sanders:
You think about warfare. There was a time, World War II, horrible wars, 50 million people died.
But you remember these brave guys, they were fighting, and that's all over. War is now going to be done by some guy pressing a button.
You're seeing what's going on in Gaza? Press a button. We can bomb an apartment building.
Who will control warfare? What's the impact of that? If I'm a president or prime minister someplace, I don't have to worry about young people coming home in body bags.
What does that mean to my views about war?

Bernie Sanders:
The Scandinavian countries have probably done best. They've done best in eliminating poverty. They've done best in providing good-quality education to all of their people.
Many of these countries, going to college or graduate school is virtually free. Healthcare is virtually free. Their campaign systems are not as corrupt as ours are in the sense that money buys power.
Some of these countries have a lot to be proud of in creating more egalitarian societies and higher standards of living and less inequality than we have in the United States.
